thread:
FinanceOps: FYI nightly NetSuite sync left a partial batch in 'processing' state and reconciliation shows 197 invoices with status mismatch (NetSuite=credit_memo, Stripe=paid). Report: /reports/billing/partial_batch_2026-03-10.csv
Noah: Investigating logs. Looks like netsuite-export job posted a batch (NS_BATCH_20260310_09) but webhook consumer for invoice.payment_succeeded processed the Stripe event after export but before the NetSuite job finished. NetSuite import idempotency only guarded by invoice_number, and some invoices were updated mid-export.
Keiko: So sequence was: Stripe event at 09:12 -> webhook consumer retried (2xx then 5xx) -> partial export at 09:13 -> import job picks partial data -> second webhook processed at 09:14 updating invoice -> result = duplicate/contradictory records.
Maya: Customers are seeing a handful of invoices with both 'paid' and 'credit memo' lines; accounting rejects automatic close. We need a safe reconciliation and a fix to prevent mid-export in-flight changes.
SRE: Root cause appears to be race between exporter and webhook processing plus a NetSuite API transient that caused exporter to retry and re-export partial file. We also found exporter didn't include a pre-checksum+signature in metadata to guarantee complete files.
Noah: Quick mitigation: pause exporter for 30m, run a reconcile that flags invoices where ns.status != stripe.status and created within export window. We'll generate CSV for manual review.
Keiko: SQL to find suspects: 
```
select ns.invoice_id, ns.status as ns_status, s.id as stripe_id, s.status as stripe_status, ns.updated_at, s.updated_at
from ns_invoices ns
join stripe_invoices s on ns.customer_id = s.customer_id and ns.invoice_number = s.number
where ns.updated_at between '2026-03-10 09:00' and '2026-03-10 09:30' and ns.status != s.status;
```
Found 197 rows.
Maya: For rollback plan: (1) mark NetSuite batch NS_BATCH_20260310_09 as 'reconcile_needed', (2) generate CSV with columns ns_invoice_id, stripe_id, suggested_action (keep_ns, keep_stripe, manual_review), confidence, reason, (3) do manual apply for high value >$500.
FinanceOps: Approve. Accounting wants proof of idempotency for any automated changes. No automated NetSuite reversals without 2 approvals.
Noah: Proposed permanent fix: exporter should write atomic file + metadata including sha256 and a 'export_in_flight' lock in DB. Webhook consumer should check export lock for a customer/export window and delay final write for 60s if lock present. Also add unique constraint on net_credit(stripe_event_id) to avoid duplicates.
SRE: We'll also harden NetSuite importer retry logic to avoid partial uploads: upload to temp folder then move/commit once complete, and include checksum verification on move.
Maya: I've started the reconcile CSV and uploaded to FIN-4512. Accounting asked to review high-dollar rows first.
deploy-bot: canary/exporter deploy started 2026-03-10T12:05Z :rocket:
Keiko: Small PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/812 (exporter atomic write + checksum), https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/813 (webhook consumer backoff-on-lock).
FinanceOps: Action items: (1) pause exporter until fixes deployed (SRE), (2) run reconcile CSV and manual review for >$500 (Maya + Accounting), (3) deploy atomic exporter + consumer backoff to staging then canary (Noah/Keiko), (4) add monitoring alert when ns/stripe status delta > 100 in 1h window.
SRE: Paused exporter at 2026-03-10T12:00Z. Will coordinate maintenance window for re-export.
FinanceOps: Keep updates here. Once reconciled, attach final audit CSV and postmortem.
